review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions and lemmas it uses: amnrWord and amnrOp in AmnrDirectional.lean, amnrWord_append, amnrWord_sum and amnrWord_sub in Calculus.lean, amnrWord_const_smul in Seed.lean, and amnrWord_add in WordLinearCalculus.lean. I also grepped the Amnr directory for @[simp] attributes and for uses of amnrWord_append inside simp calls. The amnrWord linearity lemmas carry no simp attributes and no Amnr-specific simp set exists. The only simp calls in the target are `simp only` with Pi.*_apply, smul_eq_mul, Finset.sum_fn and amnrWord_append. I did not make amnrWord_append @[simp] a finding. It is unconditional and used in simp calls in 3 files, but it changes how word applications are nested, and I found no evidence of a loop or conflict that settles the orientation. The finding below is a moderate-confidence interface-shape concern: this proof has to bridge Pi-form lemmas to lambda-form goals by hand. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim that a replacement compiles or that simp fails.

findings.excerpt: have hsub := amnrWord_sub hU hbM (hGsum.const_smul κ |>.add hFsum) hBsum w hwl hz
findings.problem: The word-linearity lemmas (amnrWord_add, amnrWord_sub, amnrWord_sum, amnrWord_const_smul) are stated for Pi-operations (`f + g`, `∑ i ∈ s, f i`, `c • f`). The goals use lambda terms (`fun z => κ * ∑ … + ∑ … - ∑ …`). So the proof needs a hand-written `change … at hsub`, `change … at hadd` and `change … at hscale`, which restate the whole lambda. It then needs several `simp only [Pi.sub_apply, smul_eq_mul]`, `[Pi.add_apply, …]` and `[Pi.smul_apply, …]` passes, and a `simp only [Finset.sum_fn] at heG heF` to turn `∑ i, f i` into a lambda sum. None of the lemmas is in a simp-friendly pointwise form, and none is a simp lemma. The same lambda restatement would recur at every call site that applies these lemmas to concrete expressions.
findings.proposed_change: Add pointwise companions next to the Pi-form lemmas in Calculus.lean and WordLinearCalculus.lean, each with the same smoothness hypotheses and `EqOn … U` conclusion. They would have the shape `amnrWord b w (fun y => f y + g y) z = amnrWord b w f z + amnrWord b w g z`, and likewise for `fun y => c * f y`, `fun y => f y - g y` and `fun y => ∑ i ∈ s, f i y`. The conclusion is pointwise, so the proof can be assembled with `rw`/`simp only` and without the three `change` restatements and the `Finset.sum_fn`/`Pi.*_apply` passes. Do not tag the hypothesis-carrying lemmas @[simp], because the smoothness side conditions are not dischargeable by simp.
findings.benefit: Callers state the lambda-form EqOn goals directly and avoid copying the long lambda in `change … at hsub/hadd/hscale`. The proof here would shrink to a short chain of `rw` steps, and the lemma statements would match how the word equations are actually written.
